content: Born into the Śākya clan through skillful means and compassion,Invincible, you who crush the hosts of Māra,With a body as majestic as a mountain of gold—To that King of the Śākyas, I prostrate.Having first aroused the mind for supreme enlightenment,You perfected the two accumulations of merit and wisdom,And now, through vast deeds for the sake of beings,I offer praise to you, who have become their protector.Knowing the time to tame those to be disciplined among the gods,You descended from the heavens and approached like a great elephant,And having observed the noble lineage, you entered the womb of Lhamo Gyutrulma—To you who did this, I prostrate.When the ten months were complete, the Son of the ŚākyasWas born in the auspicious Lumbinī Grove;To you whose supreme marks were honored by Brahmā and Indra,And who confirmed your Śākya lineage, I prostrate.You are the youthful, powerful Lion of Men,Who competed in the arts in Aṅga and Magadha;Having subdued all those who were full of pride,To you who became without rival, I prostrate.To act in accordance with the ways of the world,And to abandon any reproach, you took a retinue of consorts;To you who, through such skillful means,Governed the kingdom, I prostrate.Seeing that the activities of cyclic existence are without essence,You departed from the household and traveled through the sky;To you who ordained yourself before the Viśuddha Stūpa,I prostrate.Intending to achieve enlightenment through diligence,On the banks of the Nairañjanā for six years,You practiced austerities and perfected perseverance;To you who attained supreme meditative concentration, I prostrate.To make meaningful the efforts made since beginningless time,Beneath the Bodhi tree in Magadhā,You sat in an unmoving cross-legged posture and became a manifest Buddha;To you who perfected enlightenment, I prostrate.Having swiftly gazed upon beings with compassion,In supreme places such as Vārāṇasī,You turned the wheel of Dharma and,To you who established disciples in the three vehicles, I prostrate.In order to suppress the malicious attacks of others,The six non-Buddhist teachers, Devadatta, and the rest,You subdued as maras in the land of Vārāṇasī;To you, the Sage victorious in battle, I prostrate.With qualities unparalleled throughout the three realms,You displayed great miracles at Śrāvastī;Highly venerated by all beings, gods and humans,To you who caused the teachings to flourish, I prostrate.In order to urge the indolent toward the Dharma,Upon the pure ground of the town of Kuśinagara,You departed your immortal, vajra-like body,To you who performed the passing into nirvāṇa, I prostrate.Because in reality there is no perishing,And so that future sentient beings may accumulate merit,You emanated a wealth of relics in that very place,To you who divided your remains into eight portions, I prostrate.Thus, by the virtue of this brief praise,Of the manner of the deeds of the Buddha, the Bhagavan, the Master of the Teachings,May the conduct of all wandering beingsBecome equal to the deeds of the Sugata himself.Composed by the glorious protector Ārya Nāgārjuna.
